football_evidence.question: Can Coastal Carolina’s pass rush get to Jaxon Potter?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Coastal Carolina, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.4 of the 3.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (big plays through the air): Coastal Carolina’s offense turns 13.3% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Old Dominion’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.7% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Coastal Carolina’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 14.5% of its runs, and Old Dominion’s defense stops 16.0% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
Jaxon Potter has completed 43 of 84 passes (51.2%) for 483 yards, 5.8 yards per attempt, no touchdowns and 4 interceptions in three games for Old Dominion, and has been sacked on 10 of 94 dropbacks.
contradicting: When Coastal Carolina has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Coastal Carolina’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.3% of its dropbacks, and Old Dominion’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (big plays on the ground): Coastal Carolina’s offense turns 6.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Old Dominion’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
